title: Artificial Analysis: AI Model and API Provider Comparison Page
answer: Artificial Analysis publishes a landing page comparing AI models and API hosting providers. It describes independent benchmarks across quality, price, output speed and latency, and defines measures such as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index cost, tokens per second, and endpoint accuracy preservation. The most useful point for a healthcare reader is a limitation: the supplied text does not mention healthcare, medical reasoning, or clinical tasks, so it cannot support a claim that this page ranks models on medical tasks.

sections.body: Artificial Analysis publishes this page. It is a landing page for comparison and analysis of AI models and API hosting providers. Its stated scope is independent benchmarks across key performance metrics including quality, price, output speed and latency. The harvested text is dated 2026-09-29. It lists model developers and API providers, and it includes definitions of selected metrics. It is not a research paper, a clinical evaluation, or a healthcare-specific report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Artificial Analysis describes the page as comparison and analysis of AI models and API hosting providers. It says the benchmarks are independent and cover key performance metrics including quality, price, output speed and latency. It labels model weights as Commercial Use Restricted if commercial use is limited by conditions, and as Non-commercial if the license prohibits commercial use. It lists model providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Google, DeepSeek, Mistral and others. It notes that while model intelligence generally translates across use cases, specific evaluations may be more relevant for certain use cases. It defines the cost to run evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated using the model's input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning and answer token prices and the number of tokens used across evaluations, excluding repeats. It defines tokens per second as tokens received while the model is generating tokens, after the first chunk has been received from the API for models that support streaming. It says figures represent the model's first-party API or the median across providers where a first-party API is not available. It defines a composite measure of how much of a model's accuracy a given provider endpoint preserves, from re-running BFCL v4-500, HLE-250 and AA-LCR-25 against that endpoint. Where a self-hosted reference endpoint exists, scores are expressed as a percentage of that reference, with 100 matching the reference, and lower scores indicating accuracy lost to quantisation, sampling defaults or other endpoint-side configuration. It says scores are point-in-time snapshots and points to a methodology.

sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in healthcare would use this source to compare general model and API provider performance, cost, output speed and latency, and to understand how much accuracy an endpoint preserves. It is useful as an independent reference for broad model and hosting comparisons. It does not provide healthcare-specific evidence, so it cannot support claims about medical reasoning, clinical tasks or patient care. The source text does not rank models on medical tasks. A healthcare reader should treat it as a starting point for vendor questions and then look for separate clinical evaluations.

It is a comparison page for commercial AI models and API hosting providers, not a clinical or academic document. The harvested date is 2026-09-29, and the page may change.
